topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: When I heard the oak, the one I planted when I was but a lad, had been taken by the ax, my heart sank deeper than the roots that once clung to the earth. It was a sturdy tree, full of leaves and life, a place where I would sit and think of hopes that seemed as far as the clouds above. Now, they say the land is clear, the soil bare, but to me, a piece of the soil, a piece of my past, is gone. I know the fields need tilling, and sometimes, even the best must be sacrificed. But the sight of the empty space, where once stood a witness to my youth, leaves a hollow spot in the heart. May the saints guide the ax and the plow alike, and may the earth receive this seed of sorrow, turning it into the springing green of new days.
